lens: citations/build/gates (identifiers resolve, corrections superseded not deleted)
central_claim: The published FET-fusion -> impaired-ATM -> compensatory-ATR-dependency mechanism is internally consistent as a class claim but is NOT confirmed to transfer to EMC/EWSR1::NR4A3: the structural precondition holds for only one of EMC's three reported fusion types, public-data ATR-inhibitor sensitivity in FET-rearranged lines is not ATR-specific, and EMC tumour transcriptomes show only a WEAK (proliferation-confounded) signature -- so the wet-lab ask stands unchanged but its in-silico computational support is weaker than an earlier draft represented.

p1s.summary: The PMID/DOI for the SRP640302 EMC cohort publication (PMID 42465974, doi:10.7717/peerj.21497, cited in Part D's provenance row for `emc-sra-study.json`) could not be independently confirmed against an external index; it rests entirely on internal field-by-field cross-matching (study title, depositor name/institution, sample count, assay, prognosis split) performed in the cited sibling document rather than a fetched PubMed/CrossRef record, and network egress to pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov and doi.org is blocked in this environment so it could not be checked directly.
p1s.evidence: Pinned doc line ~872: '...publication PMID 42465974, [doi:10.7717/peerj.21497](https://doi.org/10.7717/peerj.21497))'. WebSearch for 'PMID 42465974 peerj 21497 extraskeletal myxoid chondrosarcoma' and for 'Chaiboonchoe extraskeletal myxoid chondrosarcoma PeerJ' returned no matching record. The identifier's own provenance chain is documented in research/manuscripts/fusion-output/emc-fourth-cohort-sra-2026-08-08.md Section 10 ('Update 2026-08-24'), which derives the PMID/DOI by matching STUDY_TITLE, submitter name/institution, specimen source, sample n and prognosis split between the SRA BioProject metadata and the paper -- not by reading a `pubmed`/`DOI` field out of the archive record itself (the same section states those fields are absent: 'a `PMID` | **none**', 'a `DOI` | **none**'). WebFetch to pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/doi.org returned EGRESS_BLOCKED in this sandbox.
p1s.fix: Not urgent for this pinned commit -- the cross-matching evidence (title, depositor, institution, n, assay, prognosis split all agreeing) is strong circumstantial confirmation and the identifier is not misused elsewhere in this document. When network access to PubMed/CrossRef/PeerJ is available (e.g. via the repo's Actions-runner escape hatch), do one direct esummary/CrossRef lookup on PMID 42465974 / the DOI to convert this from an internally-inferred identifier to a directly-fetched one, and record the fetch in the artifact.
